newsitem.title: USA: Edison extends San Onofre Calif. nuke outage.
newsitem.headline: Edison extends San Onofre Calif. nuke outage.

text.p: The 1,070 megawatt (MW) unit 2 at the San Onofre nuclear power plant in southern California will remain shut until March 20, a spokesman for Southern California Edison Co said Wednesday.
The unit, which was shut for planned refuelng and maintenance on November 30, was originally expected to restart early last month, but was kept out of service for further repairs.
San Onofre 2 began intial restart operations early this week but returned to cold shutdown after a pressurizer leak was discovered.
"We have determined that the leak was from an instrument nozzle," the spokesman said.
He said the nozzle will have to be replaced, testing will need to be conducted and several days of transitioning will be needed before start-up operations can resume.
San Onofre's 1,080 unit 3 continues to operate normally, but is still scheduled to begin a regular refueling outage April 5.
The plant is majority owned and operated by Edison, while Enova Corp's San Diego Gas and Electric Co owns 20 percent and the cities of Anaheim and Riverside own the remaining five percent.
